docs.text: PulseGuard Documentation Overview PulseGuard is a Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) platform developed as part of a fourth-year DevOps project. The platform monitors patient biometric telemetry, classifies health risks using predefined rules, and presents information through a clinician dashboard. The project currently consists of: Synthetic patient telemetry generation FastAPI backend services Alert classification engine React frontend dashboard Risk analysis and patient monitoring Project Goals The primary goals of PulseGuard are: Monitor patient health remotely Detect potential deterioration through telemetry analysis Support clinician decision-making Demonstrate modern DevOps practices Showcase Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD and cloud deployment strategies Technology Stack Frontend React Vite JavaScript Backend Python FastAPI Pydantic Simulation Python Requests Future Technologies PostgreSQL Docker Kubernetes Terraform GitHub Actions Prometheus Grafana Argo CD Documentation Structure The following documentation is available: Architecture Describes the system design and component interactions. See: architecture.md Setup Guide Instructions for running PulseGuard locally. See: setup.md API Documentation Details of backend endpoints and request/response formats. See: api.md Testing Documentation Testing strategy and validation procedures. See: testing.md Operations Runbook System startup and troubleshooting procedures. See: runbook.md Changelog Project history and feature progression. See: changelog.md Current Status The current prototype successfully demonstrates: Telemetry generation Telemetry ingestion Risk classification Alert processing Dashboard visualisation Real-time updates Future Work Planned enhancements include: PostgreSQL integration Authentication and authorisation Historical telemetry storage Heart rate trend visualisations Docker containerisation CI/CD automation Observability and monitoring Kubernetes deployment

docs.text: PulseGuard API Documentation Overview The PulseGuard backend exposes REST API endpoints used by the telemetry simulator and clinician dashboard. Base URL: http://127.0.0.1:8000 GET / Returns the health status of the backend service. Request GET / Response { "message": "PulseGuard Backend Running" } GET /vitals Returns stored patient telemetry readings. Request GET /vitals Example Response [ { "reading": { "patient_id": 2, "patient_name": "Sarah Smith", "heart_rate": 124, "sleep_hours": 7.2, "timestamp": "2026-11-02T15:24:47.718907" }, "alert": "HIGH RISK" } ] POST /vitals Receives telemetry from the patient simulator. Request POST /vitals Example Request Body { "patient_id": 2, "patient_name": "Sarah Smith", "heart_rate": 124, "sleep_hours": 7.2, "timestamp": "2026-11-02T15:24:47.718907" } Example Response { "message": "Vital Added" } Alert Classification Rules The backend automatically classifies patient risk levels. High Risk Heart Rate > 110 BPM Result: HIGH RISK Moderate Risk Heart Rate > 95 BPM or Sleep Hours < 5 Result: MODERATE RISK Normal Patients not matching any alert condition are classified as: NORMAL Future API Enhancements Planned API features include: Authentication Patient management endpoints Historical telemetry endpoints Alert management endpoints User roles and permissions

docs.text: PulseGuard Architecture Overview PulseGuard is a Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) platform designed to monitor patient health after discharge from hospital. The system collects biometric telemetry, processes patient readings, classifies risk levels and presents the information through a clinician dashboard. System Architecture Patient Simulator ↓ FastAPI Backend ↓ Alert Engine ↓ React Dashboard Components Patient Simulator The patient simulator generates synthetic biometric telemetry data. Example telemetry data includes: Patient ID Patient Name Heart Rate Sleep Hours Timestamp The telemetry is sent to the backend using HTTP POST requests. FastAPI Backend The backend receives telemetry from the simulator. Responsibilities: Data validation Telemetry ingestion Risk classification API endpoint exposure Current APIs: GET / GET /vitals POST /vitals Alert Engine The alert engine evaluates incoming telemetry. Current rules: Heart Rate > 110 BPM = HIGH RISK Heart Rate > 95 BPM = MODERATE RISK Sleep Hours < 5 = MODERATE RISK The generated risk level is attached to each reading. React Dashboard The dashboard retrieves telemetry using the GET /vitals endpoint. Features: Live telemetry updates Latest reading per patient Risk classification display Dashboard statistics Colour-coded patient status Current Technology Stack Frontend React Vite JavaScript Backend Python FastAPI Pydantic Simulation Python Requests Future Architecture Future development will include: PostgreSQL database Authentication Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) Docker containers CI/CD pipeline Kubernetes deployment Monitoring and logging

docs.text: PulseGuard Operations Runbook Overview This runbook provides instructions for operating and troubleshooting the PulseGuard prototype. System Startup Procedure The PulseGuard prototype consists of three components: FastAPI Backend Patient Simulator React Dashboard All three components must be running. Start Backend Navigate to: cd backend Run: uvicorn main:app --reload Expected Result: INFO: Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000 Start Simulator Open a second terminal. Navigate to: cd simulator Run: python patient_simulator.py Expected Result: Patient telemetry data is generated every few seconds. Start Dashboard Open a third terminal. Navigate to: cd frontend Run: npm run dev Expected Result: http://localhost:5173 Verification Checks Backend Check Open: http://127.0.0.1:8000 Expected Response: { "message": "PulseGuard Backend Running" } Telemetry Check Open: http://127.0.0.1:8000/vitals Expected Result: Patient telemetry records should be displayed. Dashboard Check Open: http://localhost:5173 Expected Result: Patient cards and dashboard statistics should be visible. Troubleshooting Dashboard Not Loading Data Possible Cause Backend not running. Solution Restart FastAPI: uvicorn main:app --reload No Patient Data Appears Possible Cause Simulator not running. Solution Start: python patient_simulator.py CORS Error Example Error Access to fetch has been blocked by CORS policy Solution Verify CORSMiddleware is configured in the backend. Port Already In Use Solution Terminate existing process using the port and restart the application. Future Operational Features Future versions of PulseGuard will include: PostgreSQL database Docker deployment CI/CD pipelines Logging and monitoring Kubernetes deployment Alert notifications

docs.text: PulseGuard Setup Guide Overview This guide explains how to set up and run the PulseGuard prototype locally. Prerequisites The following software must be installed: Python 3.x Node.js npm Git Clone Repository git clone https://github.com/Ibukunn7/pulseguard-prototype.git Navigate into the repository: cd pulseguard-prototype Backend Setup Navigate to the backend directory: cd backend Install dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt Start the FastAPI server: uvicorn main:app --reload The API will be available at: http://127.0.0.1:8000 Simulator Setup Open a second terminal. Navigate to the simulator directory: cd simulator Run the telemetry simulator: python patient_simulator.py The simulator will continuously generate synthetic patient telemetry data. Frontend Setup Open a third terminal. Navigate to the frontend directory: cd frontend Install dependencies: npm install Start the React application: npm run dev The dashboard will be available at: http://localhost:5173 Running the Complete System Three processes must be running simultaneously: Terminal 1 uvicorn main:app --reload Terminal 2 python patient_simulator.py Terminal 3 npm run dev Expected Behaviour The simulator generates patient telemetry. The FastAPI backend receives and classifies the data. The React dashboard displays patient status and risk levels in real time.

docs.text: PulseGuard Testing Documentation Overview Testing was performed throughout development to verify that telemetry data could successfully travel through the system and be displayed on the dashboard. Testing Strategy The current prototype uses manual testing to validate functionality. Testing focuses on: Telemetry generation API communication Alert classification Dashboard updates Test Case 1 - Backend Health Check Objective Verify that the FastAPI backend starts correctly. Steps Start the backend service. Navigate to: http://127.0.0.1:8000 Expected Result { "message": "PulseGuard Backend Running" } Result PASS Test Case 2 - Telemetry Ingestion Objective Verify that the backend receives telemetry readings. Steps Start the simulator. Monitor backend logs. Expected Result Successful POST requests appear in backend logs. Result PASS Test Case 3 - Alert Classification Objective Verify that alert rules classify patient risk correctly. Rules Tested High Risk Heart Rate > 110 BPM Expected: HIGH RISK Moderate Risk Heart Rate > 95 BPM Expected: MODERATE RISK Moderate Risk Sleep Hours < 5 Expected: MODERATE RISK Result PASS Test Case 4 - Dashboard Updates Objective Verify that the React dashboard displays incoming telemetry. Steps Start backend. Start simulator. Start frontend. Expected Result Patient information appears and updates automatically. Result PASS Test Case 5 - Dashboard Statistics Objective Verify that summary cards display accurate patient counts. Statistics Tested Total Patients Normal Patients Moderate Risk Patients High Risk Patients Result PASS Future Testing Future development will introduce: Unit testing Integration testing Automated API testing CI/CD testing pipelines Security testing Performance testing
